newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Hundreds killed in Colombian war in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds killed in Colombian war in 1996.

text.p: Colombia's internal war claimed the lives of 780 leftist guerrillas and more than 500 members of the armed forces last year, the military said in a communique Wednesday.
It said the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's oldest and largest guerrilla army, was hardest hit with 462 fighters killed in combat with the police and army.
The statement said government forces killed 248 insurgents of the National Liberation Army (ELN), the second largest rebel movement.
Two other rebel armies, the Maoist People's Liberation Army (EPL) and a dissident faction of the now defunct M-19 guerrilla movement, lost more than 60 fighters.
At least 133 police, a branch of the armed forces in Colombia, and 360 soldiers died during counterinsurgency operations and 80 were listed as missing, the communique said.
Human rights activists say that the brunt of the guerrilla war, which began more than three decades ago, falls on civilians.

More than 25,000 people were murdered in Colombia in 1996, police say. Many of these were victims of political violence but not directly linked to the armed forces, right-wing paramilitary gangs or guerrilla groups.
